answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by binding one active identity to each RPKI-signed IPv6 /48. A public ledge lists each prefix; a NAT haven behind one prefix cannot mint extra identities; an audit lantern publishes every ROA so duplicate use is visible. Enrollment needs a fresh signed challenge from that prefix's key, and the ledger rejects a second registration. Each extra identity needs another RIR-allocated prefix costing C per epoch, so total reward n(R-C), deterring only while R<C. Trust: RIRs publish allocations; a rich attacker can still lease many prefixes.
